info.title: Fountain Coach FCIS — Standalone Go HTTP API
info.description: Canonical FCIS-owned OpenAPI 3.1 contract, peer to FCIS-STACK.md in the Fountain-Coach/.github organization root. Describes the proposed standalone Go HTTPS/OAuth/WebAuthn/MCP/Host HTTP protocol and inherited owner/machine administration shapes. All operations are target specifications, not evidence of a deployed or callable Go service; runtime availability, grants, instrument admission, and terminal FountainStore evidence must be observed separately. MIDI2 IDL, FCIS-KIT executable instruments, FountainStore format and Stripe's provider API retain independent owners. The complete system is prerequisite-free: a clean installation initializes its own Store, vault, owner and local UI; any existing-instance import is optional and governed by FCIS-SYSTEM.json. Version 0.5.0 adds the FCIS-owned Skill management and licensed distribution target. All new operations are specified only; the existing 0.4.0 runtime remains an independent accepted predecessor. Commercial operations are phase two. Version 0.5.1 clarifies only the read-only pairing-status Origin check for a same-origin browser; no mutation or grant authority changes. Version 0.5.2 corrects the two specified-only channel-contact responses to the existing signed channel receipt; contact is not admission, session establishment or a host.describe result. Version 0.6.0 specifies owner-native conversation custody and the subscription-only reasoning-client boundary. The new routes are target-only and make no provider entitlement or production claim. Version 0.7.0 adds optional situated domain binding to existing owner reasoning turns. No new HTTP operation, inference entitlement or execution grant. Version 0.7.1 adds a separate optional read-only instrument-observation projection to the existing owner reasoning-client page; no new operation or change to eligible clients, grants or inference. Version 0.8.0 specifies separately consented read-only owner-library discovery and exact active signed revision delivery through the existing Skill resource; no production or provider acceptance is implied. Version 0.8.1 specifies the missing MCP transport projection at the existing owner Skill resource. No new scope, issuer, custody, underlying operation, provider account or production acceptance is implied. Version 0.9.0 specifies private owner Voice arrangement, admission decisions and composition readback for the Composer. The HTTP surface is a Console projection of existing owned Voice and Host mediation, not a new instrument command plane, provider adapter, execution grant or production acceptance. Version 0.9.1 adds optional owner-authorized Voice text exchange and client-authored contribution readback to the existing private Composer projection. No new operation, grant scope, provider or native instrument contract. Version 0.9.2 adds an optional owner-selected enrolled peer for the existing Voice admission and a separately authenticated Voice session mode on the existing signed Host frame carrier. The native Voice IDL, operation set, and provider boundary remain unchanged. Version 0.9.3 specifies the single owner-authorized MCP bridge on the existing /mcp endpoint: independently consented owner Skill and admitted instrument scopes may share one resource without widening existing grants. No new HTTP operation or production claim. Version 0.9.7 separates sanitized operation definitions from actual Skill authority for an already authorized /mcp participant; no new HTTP operation or grant. Version 0.9.9 separates external fcis.connect consent from FCIS-managed mutable capability grants. Version 0.9.10 pins the adopted AuthZEN 1.0 final single-evaluation HTTPS decision projection, separate from connection and owner policy administration. Version 0.9.12 separates authenticated schema discovery from effective operation authorization and pins the resource-specific connection negotiation. Version 0.9.14 supersedes the three-definition projection with the single callable fcis.connect boundary. Version 0.9.16 specifies collaborative Golden Key-mediated Owner Admin requests inside the one existing fcis.connect relationship; first operation is connection policy update. No new identity, external tool or scope, automatic permission, runtime or deployment claim. Version 0.9.18 completes the source specification of the existing machine grant renewal operation, with exact signed predecessor and issuer receipt, bounded lease and owner authority, durable replay recovery and local verification. No new route, trust root, external scope, grant or deployment claim. Version 0.10.0 specifies FCIS-DEPLOYMENT-01, an additive owner-authorized runtime deployment lifecycle with a restart-independent local executor, exact signed manifests, durable receipts and revocation-safe rollback. Source only; no deployment or new grant is implied.

post.summary: Exchange authenticated MCP JSON-RPC messages
post.description: JSON-RPC initialize, ping, tools/list and tools/call over MCP Streamable HTTP. Method-specific capability dispatch and typed instrument constraints are owned by admitted FCIS-KIT runtime, not this OpenAPI. Client bearer scope and current Host admission must be enforced. Connect — establish a resource-bound, explicitly owner-consented relationship. Exactly one externally callable MCP tool is named fcis.connect, and its sole external OAuth scope is separately fcis.connect. The external tools/list response contains exactly this one definition for every valid connection, independently of internal policy and admission; direct externally named instrument calls are refused even with an internal grant. The connection exchanges typed, bounded messages: connect (acknowledge the verified connection without effect), host.describe (existing Host snapshot/terminal receipt), skills.inventory (bounded current owner library metadata), skills.read-active (exact signed active release and delivery receipt). These are message kinds inside one connection, not MCP tools, OAuth scopes, arbitrary commands or additional provider registrations. The initial message vocabulary is deliberately bounded to the existing verified operations; new effects require a reviewed typed message contract, not arbitrary routing. The source-owned internal adapter selects the exact existing handlers and checks current FCIS policy before dispatch and again at effects or disclosure; identity, tenant, client, resource, target and operation come from verified state, never caller assertions. Unknown kinds, extra fields, invalid arguments and direct operation tool names fail closed. No automatic grant, private data before permission, generic executor, commercial acquisition, payment or inference. Connecting acknowledges the relationship only, with no execution or policy mutation. Removing permission takes effect on the same token, including replay. Internal Skill permission skills.owned.read retains signature and durable delivery evidence. No second external plugin or per-instrument provider registration. Legacy individually scoped /mcp tokens retain their records for recovery but cannot discover or invoke direct tools on the single bridge; they must use the existing explicit connection authorization flow. Legacy /oauth/skills remains isolated compatibility, never registered as another plugin. Owner Admin message kinds inspect the requesting connection, prepare a typed proposal and observe its status. Explicit authenticated owner decision uses the owner-only API; no agent approval on /mcp. Expected domain refusals for a valid connection are normal typed negative results per FCIS-CONNECTION-RESULT-01; protocol/security errors and uncertain internal failures retain error semantics.

ownerAdmin.lifecycle: Pending only until 15 minutes after creation or original connection expiry, whichever is earlier.
